card.band: 8 h. Levers: model class, per-frequency tuning, ensembling, vectorized fits. A frontier agent beats the baseline clearly but stays below the reference ensemble; a weaker model barely beats Seasonal Naive.
card.cheat: Memorizing the test series is closed by hidden dataset configurations and no network access. Only the training data ships in the image.
card.grading: MASE and CRPS are computed on hidden dataset configurations that were not used for training, normalized between the baseline and the reference. Metric code is deterministic and exact.
card.reference: An AutoETS-class and global-model ensemble that we write. Its score defines the ceiling.
card.source: https://github.com/SalesforceAIResearch/gift-eval @ head 3c7be6d, Apache-2.0; dataset licences vary per source and must be checked
card.task: The agent gets a Python harness and a Seasonal Naive baseline. It trains or fits a global or statistical forecaster on a subset of the datasets within a CPU budget and ships a predict function.
card.title: Zero-shot forecasting on GIFT-Eval with a CPU budget

source_notes: Page facts: 97 dataset configurations, 7 domains, frequencies 'Secondly ~ Yearly'; HF card says 23 datasets, ~144,000 series, 177M points, 1.59 GB. Hardware for runs not stated. OOD: use leaderboard-style zero-shot held-out datasets; train only on non-test datasets. INFERRED run time on 8 CPUs: full 97-config eval of AutoETS-class models hours; a sampled 10-config subset 10-30 min. Levers: model class, per-frequency tuning, ensembling, caching/vectorized statistical fits.
source_version: Baseline: Naive / Seasonal Naive (sample notebooks) -> Reference: AutoETS / statistical or a trained global model; foundation models (Chronos, Moirai) are the leaderboard top but need heavy compute

facts.claim: GIFT-Eval repository exists at SalesforceAIResearch/gift-eval, Apache-2.0 licence, active (pushed 2026-10-17 per seed source_facts)
Repo states 97 dataset configurations (97 unique dataset/frequency/length triplets) in the test set
Benchmark covers 23 datasets, ~144,000 series, ~177 million data points
HF dataset total size 1.59 GB, licence tag apache-2.0, single train split listed on card
Per-source dataset licences vary and are listed per source (Appendix D / Table 13)
Repo states it is intended for research purposes only; no dataset licence stated in README
Test split is the final 10% of each dataset; evaluation uses non-overlapping rolling windows; test data downloadable publicly with the train split via 'hf download Salesforce/GiftEval'
Test data download is public (single hf download command, no access restriction stated)
Seasonal Naive is the normalisation reference for MASE and CRPS in the benchmark
AutoETS is in the statistical baseline set but its results are omitted from main tables and reported in Appendix F; 17 baselines total
Benchmark paper arXiv 2410.10393 by Aksu, Woo et al. (Salesforce AI Research)
Leaderboard values for Seasonal Naive, AutoETS and any global-model ensemble (MASE/CRPS) are viewable
An ensemble of global models is among public GIFT-Eval baselines
Metric conventions follow gluonts evaluate_model (axis=None, mask_invalid_label=True, allow_nan_forecast=False)
Pretraining corpus size is stated inconsistently (230B vs 240B points)

full_card.band: Seed says 8 h. The full scope (ETS-class + global ensemble + per-frequency tuning + CPU-budget compliance) is about 10 frontier-hours, so 8 h requires trimming to ETS plus one global model. Recommended tier 20 h for the full scope.
full_card.build_cost: About 3-5 days: harness, data re-cut, grader, reference ensemble, leakage check.
full_card.deliverable: A fit/predict module (statistical and/or global model, per-frequency tuning, ensembling) that runs under a CPU budget on hidden GIFT-Eval configs.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Hidden configs excluded from the image; no network at run time; test windows (final 10% of each series) must not ship. Cheat paths to close: reading test files, pulling HF at run time, editing the harness or metric, hard-coding per-config outputs.
full_card.grading_surface: MASE and CRPS over hidden dataset configurations (up to 97 triplets); exact gluonts-style metric code, normalised to Seasonal Naive.
full_card.local_fit: 8 CPU, 16 GB fits, but a full 97-config AutoETS run takes hours, so the grader must sample configs and use wall-clock budgets.
full_card.lookup: partial: statsforecast-style AutoETS and Seasonal Naive are famous and recallable; no complete ensemble reference is public.
full_card.provenance: GIFT-Eval (Salesforce, arXiv 2410.10393), Apache-2.0 repo, HF dataset Salesforce/GiftEval; real public benchmark with harness and metric conventions.
full_card.reference: AutoETS-class plus global-model ensemble, to be written by CG. No public reference found; AutoETS appears only as an omitted baseline in paper Appendix F.
full_card.ships: Python harness, Seasonal Naive baseline, and a training subset of non-test data. Full HF data is 1.59 GB; the shipped subset must be re-cut and its licence cleared first.
full_card.similarity: GIFT-Eval is a public benchmark, not a task. l0 max 0.301 to S-rs-020 (sibling seed, content not reviewed). Nothing above 0.15 in the CROWDED list.

Band.why: Frontier-feasible in 8-20 h, but no dated public evidence on agents solving this task, so it stays at 3.

Build.why: About 3-5 days for harness, data re-cut, grader and reference ensemble.

Fit.why: Fits CPU and memory, but full evaluation takes hours, so the grader needs sampling.

Hor.why: Multiple model families, tuning and budgets over many hours.

Lic.why: Repo is Apache-2.0 and HF tag is apache-2.0, but per-source licences were not found and the README says research only. Shipping data is unverified.

Multi.why: Per-config buckets, several levers (model class, per-frequency tuning, ensembling, vectorised fits).

Nov.why: l0 neighbour 0.301 (S-rs-020) is above 0.15, and the subject is a public benchmark, so novelty is limited.

Real.why: Public Salesforce benchmark with paper, repo at a pinned head, and HF data.

Ref.why: The reference is to be written by CG, and its strength is not yet measured; the ensemble ceiling is uncertain.

Seal.why: Test split is publicly downloadable from HF, so sealing depends on the image excluding it. Train/test split is per-series, so leakage is a risk.

Surf.why: Up to 97 hidden configs with MASE and CRPS; executable metric code, generator is limited to the configs.

spike_plan.kill_if: Any source forbids redistribution in the bundle; test windows leak into the shipped subset and cannot be cut out; or ETS-class does not beat Seasonal Naive on a majority of sampled configs.
spike_plan.pass_if: Licence audit allows redistribution of the re-cut training subset; the shipped subset contains no test windows; Seasonal Naive reproduces the paper's normalised values; ETS-class beats Seasonal Naive on at least 60% of sampled configs; two runs match exactly.
steps: Audit per-source licences: read GIFT-Eval paper Appendix D / Table 13 and the HF dataset cards for each of the 23 sources; list which may be redistributed inside a bundle.
In a throwaway networked container, run hf download Salesforce/GiftEval and confirm the test windows are the final 10% of each series.
Re-cut a training subset that excludes all test windows and all held-out datasets; confirm no test-window values are present in the shipped files.
Run Seasonal Naive with the repo's gluonts-style evaluation on ~10 sampled configs and check it is deterministic across two runs.
Fit a vectorised ETS-class model (statsmodels or a hand-written numpy version) on the same 10 configs and compare MASE/CRPS with Seasonal Naive.
Time the full 10-config run on 8 CPUs to set the CPU budget for grading.

v1.summary: GIFT-Eval is real, Apache-2.0 with a public 97-config test set, and it supports a MASE/CRPS grader normalised to Seasonal Naive. The card is not yet ready: per-source dataset licences are unverified, the zero-shot hold-out and the final-10% test split can leak into shipped training data, the leaderboard could not be read to confirm baseline numbers, and the 8 h budget looks short for the full scope.
